summary.title: Reinvent the Wheel
summary.one_liner: Reinventing existing tools and systems as a toy version is one of the best ways to understand them, as long as you finish and then choose reuse or reinvention wisely.
keywords: build it yourself to understand it
feynman what i cannot create i do not understand
reinvent for insight reuse for impact
takeaways: Implementing a toy version of a tool or protocol is a direct way to understand it, and the result can be thrown away later.
Everyday abstractions like strings and paths are complex; building your own version reveals their tradeoffs.
Finish a project rather than jumping between projects, or you learn little.
Reuse existing work for impact and study it, but do not reinvent out of ignorance or distrust of others.
Summary advice: reinvent for insight, reuse for impact.
summary.summary: Matthias Endler argues against the common advice to never reinvent the wheel, saying it discourages curiosity. He makes the case that building a toy version of a technology (such as protocols, cryptography, web servers, strings, or paths) is the most reliable way to understand it. He lists reasons to reinvent, stresses that every design involves tradeoffs, and recommends small experiments and finishing what you start. The post closes by advising to reuse existing work for impact and reinvent for insight. It is an opinion essay with no code or tooling.
